slides.title: The Denominator Riddle
slides.narration: Welcome, young scholar. Fractions are parts of a whole, but they can only unite when their slices are the same size.

slides.title: Different Sizes Cannot Blend
slides.visual_hint: A large half-shield next to a small quarter-shield.
slides.narration: Notice the denominators: four and two. We cannot simply add one plus one to get two-sixths. That is an ancient trap!

slides.title: Summon the Common Denominator
slides.visual_hint: The half-shield dividing down the center into two quarters.
slides.narration: We can transform one-half into two-fourths. Now both fractions share the exact same denominator.

slides.title: Unite the Numerators
slides.visual_hint: One quarter-flask and two quarter-flasks pouring into a bowl.
slides.narration: Add the numerators: one plus two equals three. The denominator stays four.

slides.title: The Master Formula
slides.narration: One-fourth plus one-half equals three-fourths. You have mastered fraction addition!

slides.title: Scholar Victory
slides.visual_hint: A golden scholar badge shining on the screen.
slides.narration: Remember: always equalize denominators before adding the numerators. Onward to your next quest!
